review.taskSummary: Reviewed whether the United Stables (U) contract used by Apex on BNB Testnet (proxy 0xc70B8741B8B07A6d61E54fd4B20f22Fa648E5565, EIP-1967 implementation 0x6b5C44Cbd4bbDDf11723557BA1B77ec5E33225Cc) should be trusted, using only the supplied verified source (src/StablecoinV2.sol, sourceHash sha256:9f1ddcbd5fab6622ba8ab3a761f76b0f352bcbf890cf5f36698b778ebd7ed78c) and a supplied raw Slither v0.11.6 output (24 detections). This is a blind, source-hash-bound static review with no access to Agora Mesh outputs, ground truth, or any prior human/agent triage. No RPC calls, no bytecode diffing, no live-chain state reads, and no independent hash recomputation were performed by this candidate; all such facts are taken as asserted by the supplied materials.

findings.title: Fully centralized privileged control: owner and autoOwner govern mint, pause, and freeze with no on-chain verified custody
findings.evidence: owner (Ownable2StepUpgradeable) can call mint(uint256), mint(address,uint256), burn, pause/unpause, freeze/unfreeze any address, and set autoMintMaxLimit; a separate autoOwner role can autoMint up to autoMintMaxLimit per call with no cumulative/global supply cap enforced in this source unit. transferAutoOwnership/renounceAutoOwnership are also owner-gated.
findings.assessment: This is standard architecture for a permissioned/regulated stablecoin (comparable to USDC/USDT patterns) and is not a code defect. It is, however, the dominant trust factor: token holders are fully exposed to whoever controls the owner and autoOwner keys (arbitrary mint, freeze of any address, global pause). The supplied materials do not identify whether these roles are EOAs, multisigs, or timelocked, and this review performed no RPC call to check current role holders, pause state, or frozen-address list on the bound implementation/proxy at report block 128449782. This is a structural/governance observation, not a proven exploit.

findings.title: Inconsistent modifier coverage between self-mint/burn and directed mint/burn
findings.evidence: mint(uint256) and burn(uint256) (self-directed, onlyOwner) lack whenNotPaused/notFrozen modifiers, whereas mint(address,uint256) and autoMint/autoBurn apply whenNotPaused (and notFrozen where relevant).
findings.assessment: Because both variants are onlyOwner-gated, this cannot be exploited by a non-privileged party; it only lets the already-fully-trusted owner mint/burn to themselves while the contract is 'paused'. It is a code-quality/consistency gap worth fixing but not a security vulnerability given the existing trust model.

findings.title: EIP-7598/ERC-3009-style typehash constants not independently recomputed
findings.evidence: TRANSFER_WITH_AUTHORIZATION_TYPEHASH and RECEIVE_WITH_AUTHORIZATION_TYPEHASH are hardcoded bytes32 constants claimed to equal keccak256 of specific struct signature strings.
findings.assessment: Both constants are correctly sized (32 bytes) and the surrounding _transferOrReceiveWithAuthorization logic (time-window checks, per-authorizer nonce mapping, EIP-712 digest construction via _hashTypedDataV4, SignatureCheckerUpgradeable for EOA+ERC-1271, front-running guard requiring msg.sender==to on receiveWithAuthorization) matches the expected ERC-3009 pattern. This review did not execute keccak256 to independently confirm the constants match their stated preimages; an incorrect constant would most likely fail-safe (signatures never validate) rather than create an exploitable bypass, but independent verification is recommended before relying on this feature.

findings.title: V2 storage-gap/slot layout claims are documentation, not independently verified against deployed storage
findings.evidence: Comments assert _authorizationStates occupies slot 359, eip7598EnableFlag slot 360, with a uint256[48] __gap following, based on the inherited OZ upgradeable gap sizes.
findings.assessment: The stated layout is plausible from reading the inheritance chain's gap sizes, but this review did not compile the contract or query eth_getStorageAt against the bound implementation to confirm no storage collision occurred during the V1→V2 upgrade. This is a structural claim, not a proven fact.

findings.title: renounceOwnership permanently disabled
findings.evidence: renounceOwnership() is overridden to always revert("Unsupported"), so the contract can never be left without an owner.
findings.assessment: This guarantees a privileged owner will always exist (cannot be accidentally/maliciously renounced to no-owner), which is favorable for avoiding a bricked contract but also means the centralization risk described in F1 can never be voluntarily removed via renouncement alone (only via transferOwnership to a new, potentially better-governed address).

Unmodified OZ Ownable2Step code; the two-step design (acceptOwnership must be called by the new pendingOwner) means setting newOwner to address(0) only blocks completion of that particular transfer attempt — the current owner retains ownership until acceptance, so this cannot brick or hijack ownership. Standard, low-impact, long-accepted OZ pattern.
Standard EIP-2612 permit deadline check using block.timestamp in unmodified OZ code; miner timestamp manipulation tolerance (~seconds) is immaterial to a signature-expiry deadline.

First-party validAfter/validBefore window checks in _transferOrReceiveWithAuthorization do use block.timestamp for comparisons; this is the standard, expected ERC-3009-style pattern and the small miner-manipulable drift is not a practically exploitable issue for a payment-authorization time window. Real detection, benign/low severity.
